agent's symbols.meaning: equilibrium profile across a flat interface

agent left out.effect: Driving force for sublimation and deposition (tilting term, for example proportional to $(T-T_m)$ or vapor supersaturation, times $h(\phi)$)
agent left out.why: The work order is at coexistence, so this term is zero by assumption A1.

agent left out.effect: Anisotropy of the ice surface energy (hexagonal ice facets)
agent left out.why: Taken as isotropic (A2). The anisotropy of ice-vapor surface energy is a few percent, which is small compared with the geometric effects of pore confinement.

agent left out.effect: Regolith grain surfaces: wetting and the ice-grain and gas-grain energies
agent left out.why: The work order treats the pore space as ice plus gas only. Contact angles would enter through boundary terms, not through $f$.

agent left out.effect: Coupling to temperature and vapor density fields (latent heat, vapor diffusion)
agent left out.why: At constant uniform temperature and coexistence they do not change the equilibrium interface. They belong to the dynamics, not to this functional.

agent left out.effect: Elastic strain energy in ice and density change on phase change
agent left out.why: Ice in open pores against low-pressure gas is nearly stress-free. Elastic energy in the bulk is much smaller than $\gamma/\varepsilon$ for nanometer-to-micron $\varepsilon$.
Calibration uses a flat interface. Curved interfaces get corrections of relative order $\varepsilon/R$, which are small when $\varepsilon$ is much smaller than the pore radius $R$.
They are excluded by the deliverable. They are of relative order $(\varepsilon/L)^2$ on scales $L\gg\varepsilon$.
